main_body: farm building (barn with pitched roof and timber front wall)
top_band: red-brown shingled roof slope from row 6 to row 56 (plus chimney/vent at rows 0-8 and dormer at rows 27-50)
evidence: The main body shows a large pitched roof surface seen from above (rows 6-56, 51 rows tall) with a bright cream/tan eave trim line at rows 55-56, followed by a dark eave shadow at rows 57-59, and a vertical front wall with doors and windows from row 60 to row 92 (plus stone base to row 93). However, note the dormer roof at rows 27-38 is drawn as a flat front-facing triangle with no receding top ridge connecting to the main roof.

style.evidence: Compared to the Beodeul reference buildings on the left, the candidate's front wall (rows 60-88) consists of repetitive vertical bands of 2 flat reds without wood grain or surface speckle, and the white door/window frames and cross-braces are flat 1-2 colour fills. The roof uses a completely uniform mechanical brick-like grid repetition lacking the organic per-tile highlight variation and richness of the reference roofs. The dormer is also pasted flat onto the roof tiles like a sticker.
